plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero, eliminating all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SMH to 5% due to its downtrend and to reduce semiconductor concentration.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation and reduced volatility. It significantly lowers drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration, but also limits upside potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach and align with balanced limits.
Reduce SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to lower leveraged ETF exposure.
Add to CRWD, increasing its allocation to 10% given its strong uptrend and high score.
Initiate a new position in MRVL at 4%, a high-scoring scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some leveraged exposure while adding to quality tech.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding to strong, high-quality tech names, offering a moderate risk/reward profile.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach, while maintaining overall aggressive posture.
Increase SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6%, leaning into leveraged ETFs for higher growth potential.
Add to CRWD, increasing its allocation to 10% given its strong uptrend and high score.
Initiate new positions in MRVL at 6% and META at 5%, both high-scoring scanner setups.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk due to higher leverage and concentration in volatile assets. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can experience substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, SMH, and CRWD to zero, eliminating all leveraged and high-beta single name exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to cure the concentration breach and align with income-focused limits.
Significantly increase QQQI to 40% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.

income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions and low drawdown. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff, meaning it is not a savings account.
